transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’ve just been worrying a lot more than I used to. About work, clients, the market… my family, money. Even whether moving to the condo was the right choice. It feels like more than the situation really calls for.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get worried and keyed up, but not like… sudden intense fear that peaks right away. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you been avoiding any situations or activities because of your worries?
Not really, no. I mean… I may put things off sometimes, but I can’t think of anything I’m actually avoiding because of it.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or muscle tension?

Yes… mostly tension, I guess. By the end of the day my neck and shoulders get really tight, like I’ve been bracing myself. Sometimes I notice I’m clenching my jaw too, like when I’m driving between listings or at my desk.
Do you find that your worries are mostly about one or two specific things, or are they spread across many different areas of your life?

It’s… not just one thing. It kind of spreads around. Work stuff, clients, the market, family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It feels like I’m worrying more than the situation really calls for.
Do you feel like you can control your worrying most of the time?
Not as much as I’d like. I can tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” but then one thing turns into another… and suddenly I’ve spent half an hour going over little details I meant to drop.
Do you think your worrying is interfering with your daily life?

A little, yes. Mostly at work. Things that should be fairly routine—like going over contracts or handling a listing negotiation—take me longer than they used to. Sometimes I put off calling someone back because I’m not sure I’ve checked everything carefully enough.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
Not really most of the time, no. I mean… I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sad all the time.
Do you think your worrying is worse than what most people would worry about in the same situations?

Yes… I think so. I don’t love admitting that, but I came in because it feels like I worry about everything now—clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It feels bigger than the situation really calls for.
Do you find that you worry every day, or are there days when you don't worry at all?

Most days, yes. I don’t know that I can say it’s every single day, but it feels like there aren’t many days where something isn’t on my mind—work, family, money… that kind of thing. It just seems like more than it should be.
Do you usually find it hard to stop worrying once you've started?
Yes… sometimes. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” but then one thing leads to another, and I realize I’ve spent half an hour going over little details I was trying to let go of.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
I’m not sure. I mean… maybe at times, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really noticed feeling restless, exactly. More just… preoccupied, I guess.
Do you often feel anxious?

Yes… I think so. That’s actually why I came in. I seem to worry about almost everything lately—clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just feels like more than the situation really calls for.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to ignore them?

Yes… sort of. It’s not like one single thought exactly, but I’ll try to set something aside and then it keeps circling back. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” and then somehow one concern turns into another, and I’ve lost half an hour replaying small details I meant to let go.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive, meaning they come into your mind even when you don't want them to?

Yes… I suppose they do. I’ll try to tell myself it’s not urgent, but then one concern sort of leads to another, and before I realize it I’ve spent a long time going over little details I meant to leave alone.
Do you have thoughts that are difficult to dismiss or get rid of, even when you want to stop thinking about them?

Yes… they can be hard to shake. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” but then one concern leads into another, and suddenly I’ve spent half an hour going over little details I was trying to let go of.
Is there any area of your life where you feel you don't worry excessively?

Not really… that’s kind of why I came in. It feels like I worry about almost everything lately—work, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right choice. It just feels bigger than it should.
Do you worry about being judged or evaluated by others?
I don’t know… not especially, I think. I mean, I notice what people think sometimes, but I wouldn’t say that’s the main thing I worry about.
Do you feel like your worrying is affecting your relationships with family or friends?

A little, yes… though I notice it more with work than with friends or family. Even simple listing negotiations or contract reviews take me longer now, and sometimes I put off returning calls because I don’t feel like I’ve checked everything carefully enough.
Do you think your worries are present in nearly all aspects of your daily life?

Yes… I think so. It’s not just one thing. I seem to worry about clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It feels bigger than what’s actually going on.
